title: Phoenix Protocol: Verify Security Groups visibility using describe-security-groups (read-only, deterministic).
objectives: Understand the importance of security groups in AWS.
Learn how to verify security group visibility using the CLI.
Identify potential issues with security group configuration.

mission_brief.situation: You are operating as a secure cloud operator in an authorized sandbox where resources may or may not exist.
mission_brief.mission: Verify access safely using read-only AWS CLI commands without assuming any pre-existing resources.
mission_brief.execution: Run discovery-only commands and validate success by deterministic behavior (successful execution), not resource presence.

content.concept: Security groups are a fundamental component of AWS security. They act as virtual firewalls that control inbound and outbound traffic to instances. To ensure secure cloud operations, it is essential to verify the visibility of these security groups.
content.walkthrough: To verify security group visibility using the CLI, navigate to the EC2 dashboard and select 'Security Groups' from the left-hand menu. Click on the three dots next to a security group name and choose 'Actions' > 'Describe Security Group'. This will display detailed information about the selected security group.
checkpoints: Verify that the security group is correctly associated with instances.
Check for any unauthorized inbound or outbound rules.
Ensure that the security group has the correct VPC association.
common_mistakes: Misunderstanding the purpose of security groups.
Not verifying security group visibility regularly.

lab.setup: Ensure AWS CLI is configured with sandbox credentials. Do not create, modify, or delete any resources.
safety: Use read-only AWS CLI commands only (list/describe/get).
Do not reference named resources unless the lesson explicitly created them (this v2 track does not).
If you see AccessDenied, stop and verify permissions rather than trying write actions.

elite_competence.role_simulation: Demonstrate understanding of security group configuration and visibility.

bug_injection.bug: Operator assumes resources must exist and mislabels empty output as failure.
bug_injection.symptom: Student reports 'nothing returned' and believes permissions are broken.
bug_injection.fix: Explain empty-sandbox behavior and validate by successful execution + no errors, not by finding assets.

pass_conditions: Describe Security Group command executed without errors.
fail_conditions: Security group not associated with instances.

interrogation_questions: What is the purpose of security groups in AWS?
How do you verify security group visibility using the CLI?
What are common mistakes to avoid when configuring security groups?

legal_context.allowed: Executing read-only AWS CLI commands in an authorized sandbox or training account.
legal_context.prohibited: Creating, deleting, or modifying AWS resources without explicit authorization.

resume_bullets: Identified and addressed security group configuration issues.
Verified security group visibility using the CLI.
Developed expertise in security group management best practices.
